title: Arrays as Function Args
concept: When passing an array to a function, only the 'address' is actually passed, not the entire array.

steps.title: with header
steps.explanation:
Use the output function with `#include <stdio.h>`.

The key point this time is that when passing an array as a function argument, the starting address is passed, not the entire array.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created and then initializes the array.

`printSize` has not yet been called, and the goal is to observe the data transfer form when called.

steps.title: Array initialization
steps.explanation:
`nums` initializes 5 ints into contiguous memory.

The important point is that this entire block is not copied when the function is called.

steps.title: output sizeof in main
steps.explanation:
In main, `sizeof(nums)` returns the total size of the array.

Comparing this value to the result of `sizeof(arr)` inside the function reveals the difference in decay.

steps.title: Function calls and Array Decay
steps.explanation:
When calling `printSize(nums);`, `nums` is decayed and passed to the address `&nums[0]`.

That is, the function receives the starting position of the original array, not a copy of the array.

steps.title: sizeof betrayal
steps.explanation:
The function parameter `arr` behaves as a pointer, so `sizeof(arr)` returns the size of the pointer variable.

Therefore, the original array length cannot be known just from inside the function, so the length argument must be passed as well.

steps.title: Original can be destroyed
steps.explanation:
`arr[0] = 999;` directly replaces the original `nums[0]` of main through the received address.

If you want to prevent modification of the original, use a read-only parameter like `const int arr[]`.
steps.stdout:
Inside main: 20
Inside func: 8
After func: 999

steps.title: Check original changes
steps.explanation:
If you print `nums[0]` in main, the changed value will be visible as is.

In summary, array argument passing is "address passing", and length and modifiability management are key.
steps.stdout:
Inside main: 20
Inside func: 8
After func: 999

quiz.question: What if you want to know the number of elements in an array in a function?
options: There is no way to know
quiz.explanation:
Inside the function, it degenerates into a pointer, so the `sizeof` trick does not work.
You must always receive a number (`int size`) as an argument.

misconceptions.wrong: If you write `int arr[10]` in the parameter, an array of 10 items will be copied.
misconceptions.correct: The number 10 is ignored and just becomes `int *arr`.
misconceptions.why:
The C language does not automatically copy arrays.
It only serves as a comment to give hints to the programmer.

keyTakeaway: When passing an array to a function, only the 'address' goes. Be sure to include the length as well.
